about: Hand-curated supermassive black holes for Space Maps (object framework section 18.8). Every number carries `src` (a key of `papers`) and `where` (the passage, table or equation it was read from, re-read in the paper text on 2026-11-19); the build refuses any number without both. Each black hole sits at the centre of its host galaxy record (`host_galaxy`), whose position and distance the build copies from the built `galaxies` dataset, so a black hole and its galaxy never have two distances. `assumed_dist` is the distance the mass paper assumed or measured; it is shown on the card as not used. When `rescale` is true the mass is multiplied by D_adopted / D_assumed, because a dynamical mass scales linearly with the assumed distance (`scaling` quotes where the paper says so). These records hold no Gaia values and no Gaia-licensed data.

eht2019a.cite: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration 2019, ApJL 875, L1 (Paper I)

eht2019f.cite: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration 2019, ApJL 875, L6 (Paper VI)

vdbosch2010.cite: van den Bosch & de Zeeuw 2010, MNRAS 401, 1770

black_holes.name: M87*
black_holes.state: accreting: the EHT ring and a relativistic jet
black_holes.method_text: mass from the size of the black hole's shadow (Event Horizon Telescope)

mass.where: abstract and Sec. 9.2: M = 6.5 ± 0.2 (stat) ± 0.7 (sys) × 10^9 Msun; Table 7, last row

assumed_dist.where: Sec. 8.1: 'we adopt a distance of D = 16.8 +0.8 −0.7 Mpc to M87' (one TRGB and two SBF measurements; Table 9)

scaling.where: abstract: the angular gravitational radius GM/Dc^2 = 3.8 ± 0.4 μas is measured, so M ∝ D; Appendix I.2: dynamical masses 'measure, in reality, a mass-to-distance ratio'

ring_diameter.where: abstract: 'an asymmetric bright emission ring with a diameter of 42±3 μas'

black_holes.name: NGC 4258*
black_holes.method_text: mass from the orbits of water masers in its disc

mass.where: Table 2 (Fitted Disk Model), 'Black hole mass (10^7 Msun) 3.98 ± 0.04'

assumed_dist.where: abstract: 'we find the distance to NGC 4258 to be 7.576 ± 0.082 (stat.) ± 0.076 (sys.) Mpc'

scaling.where: the maser model fits the mass and the distance together (Table 2); the mass at a given distance scales as M ∝ D for the same rotation curve

black_holes.name: M31*
black_holes.method_text: mass from the motions of stars in its nucleus (P3 disc)

mass.where: abstract: 'the best fit and the lowest black hole mass are obtained for a thin disk model with M• = 1.4 × 10^8 Msun ... the 1-σ confidence range becomes (1.1 to 2.3) ×10^8 Msun'

black_holes.no_rescale_reason: Bender et al. 2005 do not state the distance they assumed, so the mass is shown as published and not rescaled.

black_holes.name: M32*
black_holes.method_text: mass from the motions of stars in its centre

mass.where: Sec. 3.1.2 and Conclusions: 'our M• mass estimate of (2.4±1.0)×10^6 Msun'

assumed_dist.where: Sec. 3.1: 'For our modeling of M32 we assumed a distance of 0.79 Mpc'

scaling.where: orbit-based dynamical model at an assumed distance (Sec. 3.1); a dynamical mass scales as M ∝ D

black_holes.name: Cen A*
black_holes.method_text: mass from the motions of stars in its centre

mass.where: abstract: 'MBH = (5.5 ± 3.0) × 10^7 Msun (3σ errors)'; stored as 1σ = 3.0/3 = 1.0 × 10^7, the paper's 3σ error divided by 3

assumed_dist.where: Sec. 2: 'Here we adopt a value D = 3.5 Mpc to be consistent with all the earlier papers on MBH determination on this galaxy'

scaling.where: footnote 2: 'lengths and masses scale as D, while mass-to-light ratios scale as D^−1'

black_holes.name: M81*
